title: सामुदायिक माध्यमिक विद्यालयहरूको कार्यसम्पादन स्तर
nepali: विद्यालय सुधार योजना निर्माण, शैक्षणिक योजना निर्माण, शिक्षणमा प्रविधिको प्रयोग, शिक्षकहरुलाई पेसागत विकासका अवसरहरु, विद्यालयको दुरदृष्टि, सोच तथा लक्ष्यहरु सार्वजनिक, विषयगत सिकाई उपलब्धिमा सुधार, विद्यार्थी डायरी व्यवस्थापन, विद्यार्थी आचार संहिता, शिक्षकलाई प्रोत्साहन÷पुरस्कार र कार्यसम्पादन स्तरका आधारमा विद्यालयलाई सहयोग प्रदान गर्ने जस्ता कार्यहरु सबै विद्यालयमा हुनुपर्ने देखिन्छ । विद्यालय समुदायको हो र समुदायको दीर्घकालिन विकास विद्यालयबाट नै हुन्छ भन्ने भावना राखी सक्रियताका साथ विद्यालयको समग्र स्तरको सुधारमा प्र.अ., शिक्षक, अभिभावक, विद्यार्थी लगायत स्थानीय निकायहरु, प्रदेश र संघको भूमिका महत्वपूर्ण हुन्छ ।  त्यसैगरी प्रत्येक वर्ष विद्यालयको कार्यसम्पादनको मूल्याङ्कन गाउँपालिकाले खटाएको विशेषज्ञ टोलीबाट गर्न लगाई सुधारका लागि पृष्ठपोषण सहितको कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्नु आवश्यक देखिन्छ । विद्यालयले वृद्धि गरेको शैक्षिक गुणस्तर सूचकहरुको आधारमा आर्थिक अनुदान र अन्य सुविधाहरु बढाउँदै जानु उपयुक्त हुन्छ । गाउँपालिका भरीका विद्यालयको (५–९) कक्षाको परीक्षा गाउँपालिकाको शिक्षा शाखाले सञ्चालन गर्ने । विद्यालयमा खेल शिक्षक र कम्प्युटर शिक्षकको दरबन्दी सृजना र जनशक्ति व्यवस्थापनका लागि प्रदेश र संघले नीतिगत व्यवस्था गर्नु पर्ने देखिन्छ, विद्यालय सुधार योजना बनाउन गाउँपालिकाले विज्ञ समूह पठाई सरोकारवालाहरुको सहभागितामा निर्माण गर्ने जसले गर्दा वास्तविक अवस्था, सुधार गर्नुपर्ने पक्ष, स्रोत साधन, पूँजी आदिको यथार्थ अवस्था प्राप्त भई सुधारात्मक कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्न स्थानीय निकायलाई आधार प्राप्त हुन्छ । थुलुङ दुधकोशी गाउँपालिकाका ९ वटा माध्यमिक विद्यालयलाई स्थानीय स्रोत, साधन र आवश्यकताका आधारमा प्राविधिक र व्यवसायिक शिक्षालयको रुपमा विकास गर्दै लानु पर्ने देखिन्छ । साथै  नमुना विद्यालयको भ्रमण र तालिमका लागि प्रदेश सरकारले वि.व्य.स.का पदाधिकारीहरु, शिक्षक अभिभावक संघ र शिक्षकहरुलाई अवसर प्रदान गर्नु पर्दछ, जसले गर्दा कार्यसम्पादनको स्तर बढ्ने देखिन्छ । संघीय सरकारले भौतिक पूर्वाधार, शिक्षक व्यवस्थापन, शैक्षिक सामग्री, ल्याब, पुस्तकालय, खेल सामग्री लगायतका विद्यालयमा हुनुपर्ने न्यूनतम मापदण्ड तयार गर्ने, बजेट व्यवस्थापन गर्ने साथै यसको रेखदेख अनुगमन र पृष्ठपोषण स्थानीय सरकारबाट गर्दा विद्यालयको कार्यसम्पादन स्तरमा थप सुधार गर्न सकिने देखिन्छ ।
american_english: Activities such as preparing school improvement plans, preparing educational plans, use of technology in teaching, opportunities for professional development of teachers, making the school's vision, thinking and goals public, improvement in subject-wise learning achievement, management of student diaries, student code of conduct, encouragement/reward for teachers and providing support to schools on the basis of performance level — all such activities should be present in every school, it appears. Holding the sentiment that the school belongs to the community and that the community's long-term development takes place through the school itself, the role of the head teacher, teachers, parents, students along with local bodies, province and federation in actively improving the overall level of the school is important. Similarly, it appears necessary that each year the evaluation of the school's performance be got done by an expert team deputed by the rural municipality, and a programme with feedback for improvement be run. It is appropriate that financial grants and other facilities be increased on the basis of the educational quality indicators the school has raised. The education section of the rural municipality should conduct the (5–9) class examination of schools across the rural municipality. It appears that the province and the federation should make policy arrangements for the creation of posts for physical education teachers and computer teachers and for human resource management in schools, and that the rural municipality should send an expert group to prepare the school improvement plan with the participation of stakeholders, whereby the real situation, aspects needing improvement, resources and funds and the like are ascertained, giving the local body a basis to run corrective programmes. It appears that the 9 secondary schools of Thulung Dudhkoshi rural municipality should be developed into technical and vocational education centres on the basis of local resources, means and needs. Also, the provincial government should provide opportunities for visits and training at model schools to officials of the school management committee, the teacher-parent association and teachers, whereby the level of performance is seen to increase. It appears that if the federal government prepares the minimum standards that should exist in schools — physical infrastructure, teacher management, educational materials, labs, libraries, sports materials and the like — manages the budget, and has monitoring, supervision and feedback carried out by the local government, further improvement in the performance level of schools can be made.

informal_english: Look, every school should really have all these things going on — school improvement plans, education plans, using tech in teaching, chances for teachers to grow professionally, making the school's vision and goals public, better subject-wise learning, student diaries, a student code of conduct, rewards for teachers, and support based on how the school performs. The school belongs to the community, and the community's long-term development happens through it, so the head teacher, teachers, parents, students, local bodies, the province and the centre all have a big role in lifting the school's overall level. Each year, the rural municipality should get an expert team to evaluate the school's performance and run a feedback-based improvement programme. It makes sense to bump up grants and facilities as the school's quality indicators improve. The rural municipality's education section should handle the classes 5 to 9 exams for all schools in the area. The province and the centre should make policy for creating posts for PE and computer teachers and managing staff, and the rural municipality should send an expert group to draft the school improvement plan with stakeholders so the real picture — what needs fixing, resources, funds — is clear, giving the local body a basis for corrective work. The nine secondary schools of Thulung Dudhkoshi rural municipality should be developed into technical and vocational institutes based on local needs and resources. The provincial government should give SMC officials, teacher-parent associations and teachers chances to visit and train at model schools, which should push performance up. And if the federal government sets minimum standards for schools — infrastructure, teachers, materials, labs, libraries, sports stuff — manages the budget, and has the local government handle monitoring and feedback, school performance can improve further.
